=== Wizard Duel of Three ===

DECK (32 cards). Four suits, Red (R), Blue (B), Green (G) and Yellow (Y), each numbered 1 to 7 (28 cards), plus 2 Wizards (W1, W2) and 2 Jesters (J1, J2). Cards are written as suit letter and number, e.g. R5.

STRUCTURE. The game has 6 hands. Each hand has 5 tricks, and each trick is one game round, so the game lasts exactly 30 rounds. Seats are 1, 2 and 3. The dealer of hand 1 is seat 1, and the dealer moves to the next seat (1, then 2, then 3, then 1) each hand.

START OF A HAND (first trick of each hand only). (a) The deck is rebuilt from all 32 cards and shuffled. (b) Each player receives 5 cards, kept privately. (c) The next card is turned face up and announced. If it is a numbered card, its suit is trump for this hand. If it is a Wizard or a Jester, there is no trump this hand. (d) The 16 remaining cards are not used this hand and nobody sees them. (e) Each player's bid and tricks taken are reset to 0. (f) All three players, at the same moment and without seeing each other's choice, bid how many of the 5 tricks they will take: 0 to 5. The bids need not add up to 5. (g) All bids are then announced, one message per player. The player after the dealer leads the first trick.

EACH TRICK. (1) The led suit is reset to none and the trick is empty. (2) The leader plays any one card from their hand, face up. (3) The next player in seat order plays any one card from their hand. (4) The third player plays any one card from their hand. There is no obligation to follow suit: any card in hand may always be played, and the played card leaves your hand. The led suit is the suit of the first numbered card played in the trick. A Jester played before it does not set the suit. If a Wizard is the first card played, the trick has no led suit, and that Wizard wins.

WHO WINS THE TRICK. If any Wizard was played, the first Wizard played wins. Otherwise, if any trump was played, the highest trump wins. Otherwise, the highest card of the led suit wins. If all three cards are Jesters, the first Jester played wins. Numbered cards not of the led suit and not trump can never win. Every card is unique, so there are no ties. The winner's tricks taken increases by 1 and is announced, and the winner leads the next trick.

END OF A HAND (after the fifth trick). Each player's score changes: if tricks taken equals the bid exactly, the player gains 20 + 10 x tricks taken (bid 2 and took 2 gives +40; bid 0 and took 0 gives +20). Otherwise, the player loses 10 x |bid - tricks taken| (bid 3 and took 1 gives -20). Each player's trick count and new score are announced in separate messages, then the dealer moves to the next seat.

INFORMATION. You see your own hand, the turned trump card, all revealed bids, every card played so far, and all scores. You never see other players' hands or the unused cards. There is no discussion phase.

END. After the 30th trick (the end of hand 6), the game ends. The player with the highest score wins. If two or three players tie for the highest score, those players share the win and the game is a draw.

STRUCTURE. The game has 6 hands. Each hand has 5 tricks, and each trick is one game round, so the game lasts exactly 30 rounds. Seats are 1, 2 and 3. The dealer of hand 1 is seat 1, and the dealer moves to the next seat (1, then 2, then 3, then 1) each hand.

START OF A HAND (first trick of each hand only). (a) The deck is rebuilt from all 32 cards and shuffled. (b) Each player receives 5 cards, kept privately. (c) The next card is turned face up and announced. If it is a numbered card, its suit is trump for this hand. If it is a Wizard or a Jester, there is no trump this hand. (d) The 16 remaining cards are not used this hand and nobody sees them. (e) Each player's bid and tricks taken are reset to 0. (f) All three players, at the same moment and without seeing each other's choice, bid how many of the 5 tricks they will take: 0 to 5. The bids need not add up to 5. (g) All bids are then announced, one message per player. The player after the dealer leads the first trick.

EACH TRICK. (1) The led suit is reset to none and the trick is empty. (2) The leader plays any one card from their hand, face up. (3) The next player in seat order plays any one card from their hand. (4) The third player plays any one card from their hand. There is no obligation to follow suit: any card in hand may always be played, and the played card leaves your hand. The led suit is the suit of the first numbered card played in the trick. A Jester played before it does not set the suit. If a Wizard is the first card played, the trick has no led suit, and that Wizard wins.

WHO WINS THE TRICK. If any Wizard was played, the first Wizard played wins. Otherwise, if any trump was played, the highest trump wins. Otherwise, the highest card of the led suit wins. If all three cards are Jesters, the first Jester played wins. Numbered cards not of the led suit and not trump can never win. Every card is unique, so there are no ties. The winner's tricks taken increases by 1 and is announced, and the winner leads the next trick.

START OF A HAND (first trick of each hand only). (a) The deck is rebuilt from all 32 cards and shuffled. (b) Each player receives 5 cards, kept privately. (c) The next card is turned face up and announced. If it is a numbered card, its suit is trump for this hand. If it is a Wizard or a Jester, there is no trump this hand. (d) The 16 remaining cards are not used this hand and nobody sees them. (e) Each player's bid and tricks taken are reset to 0. (f) All three players, at the same moment and without seeing each other's choice, bid how many of the 5 tricks they will take: 0 to 5. The bids need not add up to 5. (g) All bids are then announced, one message per player. The player after the dealer leads the first trick.

EACH TRICK. (1) The led suit is reset to none and the trick is empty. (2) The leader plays any one card from their hand, face up. (3) The next player in seat order plays any one card from their hand. (4) The third player plays any one card from their hand. There is no obligation to follow suit: any card in hand may always be played, and the played card leaves your hand. If a Wizard is the first card played, the trick has no led suit, and that Wizard wins.

The winner's tricks taken increases by 1 and is announced, and the winner leads the next trick.

=== Wizard Duel of Three ===

DECK (32 cards). Four suits, Red (R), Blue (B), Green (G) and Yellow (Y), each numbered 1 to 7 (28 cards), plus 2 Wizards (W1, W2) and 2 Jesters (J1, J2). Cards are written as suit letter and number, e.g. R5.

STRUCTURE. The game has 6 hands. Each hand has 5 tricks, and each trick is one game round, so the game lasts exactly 30 rounds. Seats are 1, 2 and 3. The dealer of hand 1 is seat 1, and the dealer moves to the next seat (1, then 2, then 3, then 1) each hand.

START OF A HAND (first trick of each hand only). (a) The deck is rebuilt from all 32 cards and shuffled. (b) Each player receives 5 cards, kept privately. (c) The next card is turned face up and announced. If it is a numbered card, its suit is trump for this hand. If it is a Wizard or a Jester, there is no trump this hand. (d) The 16 remaining cards are not used this hand and nobody sees them. (e) Each player's bid and tricks taken are reset to 0. (f) All three players, at the same moment and without seeing each other's choice, bid how many of the 5 tricks they will take: 0 to 5. The bids need not add up to 5. (g) All bids are then announced, one message per player. The player after the dealer leads the first trick.

EACH TRICK. (1) The led suit is reset to none and the trick is empty. (2) The leader plays any one card from their hand, face up. (3) The next player in seat order plays any one card from their hand. (4) The third player plays any one card from their hand. There is no obligation to follow suit: any card in hand may always be played, and the played card leaves your hand. The led suit is the suit of the first numbered card played in the trick. A Jester played before it does not set the suit. If a Wizard is the first card played, the trick has no led suit, and that Wizard wins.

WHO WINS THE TRICK. If any Wizard was played, the first Wizard played wins. Otherwise, if any trump was played, the highest trump wins. Otherwise, the highest card of the led suit wins. If all three cards are Jesters, the first Jester played wins. Numbered cards not of the led suit and not trump can never win. Every card is unique, so there are no ties. The winner's tricks taken increases by 1 and is announced, and the winner leads the next trick.

END OF A HAND (after the fifth trick). Each player's score changes: if tricks taken equals the bid exactly, the player gains 20 + 10 x tricks taken (bid 2 and took 2 gives +40; bid 0 and took 0 gives +20). Otherwise, the player loses 10 x |bid - tricks taken| (bid 3 and took 1 gives -20). Each player's trick count and new score are announced in separate messages, then the dealer moves to the next seat.

INFORMATION. You see your own hand, the turned trump card, all revealed bids, every card played so far, and all scores. You never see other players' hands or the unused cards. There is no discussion phase.

END. After the 30th trick (the end of hand 6), the game ends. The player with the highest score wins. If two or three players tie for the highest score, those players share the win and the game is a draw.

[user]
=== Wizard Duel of Three ===

DECK (32 cards). Four suits, Red (R), Blue (B), Green (G) and Yellow (Y), each numbered 1 to 7 (28 cards), plus 2 Wizards (W1, W2) and 2 Jesters (J1, J2). Cards are written as suit letter and number, e.g. R5.

STRUCTURE. The game has 6 hands. Each hand has 5 tricks, and each trick is one game round, so the game lasts exactly 30 rounds. Seats are 1, 2 and 3. The dealer of hand 1 is seat 1, and the dealer moves to the next seat (1, then 2, then 3, then 1) each hand.

START OF A HAND (first trick of each hand only). (a) The deck is rebuilt from all 32 cards and shuffled. (b) Each player receives 5 cards, kept privately. (c) The next card is turned face up and announced. If it is a numbered card, its suit is trump for this hand. If it is a Wizard or a Jester, there is no trump this hand. (d) The 16 remaining cards are not used this hand and nobody sees them. (e) Each player's bid and tricks taken are reset to 0. (f) All three players, at the same moment and without seeing each other's choice, bid how many of the 5 tricks they will take: 0 to 5. The bids need not add up to 5. (g) All bids are then announced, one message per player. The player after the dealer leads the first trick.

EACH TRICK. (1) The led suit is reset to none and the trick is empty. (2) The leader plays any one card from their hand, face up. (3) The next player in seat order plays any one card from their hand. (4) The third player plays any one card from their hand. There is no obligation to follow suit: any card in hand may always be played, and the played card leaves your hand. The led suit is the suit of the first numbered card played in the trick. A Jester played before it does not set the suit. If a Wizard is the first card played, the trick has no led suit, and that Wizard wins.

WHO WINS THE TRICK. If any Wizard was played, the first Wizard played wins. Otherwise, if any trump was played, the highest trump wins. Otherwise, the highest card of the led suit wins. If all three cards are Jesters, the first Jester played wins. Numbered cards not of the led suit and not trump can never win. Every card is unique, so there are no ties. The winner's tricks taken increases by 1 and is announced, and the winner leads the next trick.

END OF A HAND (after the fifth trick). Each player's score changes: if tricks taken equals the bid exactly, the player gains 20 + 10 x tricks taken (bid 2 and took 2 gives +40; bid 0 and took 0 gives +20). Otherwise, the player loses 10 x |bid - tricks taken| (bid 3 and took 1 gives -20). Each player's trick count and new score are announced in separate messages, then the dealer moves to the next seat.

INFORMATION. You see your own hand, the turned trump card, all revealed bids, every card played so far, and all scores. You never see other players' hands or the unused cards. There is no discussion phase.

END. After the 30th trick (the end of hand 6), the game ends. The player with the highest score wins. If two or three players tie for the highest score, those players share the win and the game is a draw.

START OF A HAND (first trick of each hand only). (a) The deck is rebuilt from all 32 cards and shuffled. (b) Each player receives 5 cards, kept privately. === Wizard Duel of Three ===

DECK (32 cards). Four suits, Red (R), Blue (B), Green (G) and Yellow (Y), each numbered 1 to 7 (28 cards), plus 2 Wizards (W1, W2) and 2 Jesters (J1, J2). Cards are written as suit letter and number, e.g. R5.

STRUCTURE. The game has 6 hands. Each hand has 5 tricks, and each trick is one game round, so the game lasts exactly 30 rounds. Seats are 1, 2 and 3. The dealer of hand 1 is seat 1, and the dealer moves to the next seat (1, then 2, then 3, then 1) each hand.

START OF A HAND (first trick of each hand only). (a) The deck is rebuilt from all 32 cards and shuffled. (b) Each player receives 5 cards, kept privately. (c) The next card is turned face up and announced. If it is a numbered card, its suit is trump for this hand. If it is a Wizard or a Jester, there is no trump this hand. (d) The 16 remaining cards are not used this hand and nobody sees them. (e) Each player's bid and tricks taken are reset to 0. (f) All three players, at the same moment and without seeing each other's choice, bid how many of the 5 tricks they will take: 0 to 5. The bids need not add up to 5. (g) All bids are then announced, one message per player. The player after the dealer leads the first trick.

EACH TRICK. (1) The led suit is reset to none and the trick is empty. (2) The leader plays any one card from their hand, face up. (3) The next player in seat order plays any one card from their hand. (4) The third player plays any one card from their hand. There is no obligation to follow suit: any card in hand may always be played, and the played card leaves your hand. The led suit is the suit of the first numbered card played in the trick. A Jester played before it does not set the suit. If a Wizard is the first card played, the trick has no led suit, and that Wizard wins.

If all three cards are Jesters, the first Jester played wins. Numbered cards not of the led suit and not trump can never win. Every card is unique, so there are no ties. The winner's tricks taken increases by 1 and is announced, and the winner leads the next trick.

(d) The 16 remaining cards are not used this hand and nobody sees them. (e) Each player's bid and tricks taken are reset to 0. (f) All three players, at the same moment and without seeing each other's choice, bid how many of the 5 tricks they will take: 0 to 5. The bids need not add up to 5. (g) All bids are then announced, one message per player. The player after the dealer leads the first trick.

EACH TRICK. (1) The led suit is reset to none and the trick is empty. (2) The leader plays any one card from their hand, face up. (3) The next player in seat order plays any one card from their hand.
